title: Adding min()/max()/sum()/avg() aggregates wrapped the caller-supplied column name in sqlalchemy.text() with no check that it is a real model field, so a crafted column string injects SQL into the aggregate query.

findings.explanation: The new validation code checks that field_name exists in model_fields before use. This prevents SQL injection via arbitrary column names. The check `x.field_name not in x.target_model.model_fields` enforces an allowlist of valid fields, preventing user-controlled input from reaching SQL queries as raw column references.

The change adds a validation layer to prevent arbitrary field access through aggregate functions. By restricting operations to only fields defined in model_fields, it prevents information disclosure through IDOR-style attacks where a user could query arbitrary columns. The validation does not bypass existing authorization checks—it adds an additional input validation gate.

evidence.content:
@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_arbitrary_sql_execution():
    async with base_ormar_config.database:
        async with base_ormar_config.database.transaction(force_rollback=True):
            if not await Item.objects.count():
                cat = await Category.objects.create(name="Electronics")
                await Item.objects.create(name="Tablet", price=449.99, category=cat)
                await Item.objects.create(name="Monitor", price=329.99, category=cat)

            column = "1 + 1"
            with pytest.raises(ormar.exceptions.QueryDefinitionError):
                await Item.objects.min(column)
